correctness.rationale: For real symmetric stochastic kernels the objective on the constants' orthogonal complement is the convex norm ||P−J||₂; automorphism averaging is legitimate even if the optimizer itself is not orbit-invariant. There are precisely two orbit weights a≤1/q and b≤1/p, with subdivision holding nonnegative throughout their rectangle. Decomposing the p×q edge-vertex array into constant, row-only, column-only and doubly centered parts yields the stated dimensions and spectra. At saturation the nonstationary constant-sector eigenvalues are 0 and −s, with s=1/p+1/q; row and column blocks have off-diagonals 1/√q and 1/√p and common diagonal pair 0, 1−s. Hence the saturated SLEM is max(F,s), where F is the positive root of x²−(1−s)x−1/p. The sign polynomial 2s²−s−1/p is negative throughout the allowed s interval for p≥3 (convex with both endpoints negative), and for p=2,q≥4 (increasing there, with value −1/8 at 3/4). It is positive in precisely the two stated exceptions. For any orbit weights the saturated F-eigenvector with entries 0 on U, t_j on V, and Ft_j on W for nonzero zero-sum t tests the Laplacian. Its squared edge differences summed in each orbit are strictly positive since 0<F<1; lowering either weight strictly reduces its quotient below 1−F. Thus saturation is uniquely optimal among averaged weights in the main range and every unrestricted optimizer has zero original holding, by nonnegativity of the averaged diagonals. In the exceptions adding a small identity component strictly decreases the unique active modulus −s, while all others have strict slack; zero original holding would average back to the nonoptimal saturated matrix. Implicit differentiation at 1/q=0 gives the coefficient p/(p+1). No unrestricted matrix uniqueness or exceptional optimum values are assumed. The frozen spectral/threshold verifier was inspected but not executed; the exact decomposition and Rayleigh argument prove the result for all parameters.

evidence: Averaging guarantees existence in the fixed subspace, not that every optimizer saturates even one orbit's diagonals. The pendant rigidity result uses leaves with private degree-one incidences; subdivision vertices here have degree two and are shared by precisely two originals.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new implication uses strictness of a Rayleigh quotient simultaneously in both edge orbits and a negative eigenvalue comparison depending on s. Neither follows merely from solving generic FMMC by SDP, from the unsplit edge-transitive formula, nor by substituting the degrees into a pendant-leaf theorem.

evidence: The graph here is the vertex–edge incidence graph of K_p,q, which inserts a different degree-two vertex for each pair. The closest indexed complete-bipartite result, 203d7ad904b3, uses quadratic Laplacian kernels on the unsplit graph. Jafarizadeh's layered graphs use full connections between specified layers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An unsplit graph with one edge orbit or a restriction to quadratic polynomials in the unsplit Laplacian is not an alias for the subdivided one-step model. Holding and the negative constant-sector eigenvalue are measured on a different state space.

value.rationale: An exact fastest-mixing solution on this natural family decides when complete use of the original rows is optimal, even for optimizers that break graph symmetries. The two smallest exceptions isolate the competing negative mode, and the explicit formula resolves the fixed-small-part gap scale. This is more than a finite numerical minimization or an orbit count.
